initial_gap: preflight_assets could publish any scheduled run, and stage_released_run could stage it, while audit_run_receipts detected block-order violations only after declared attempts existed.

local_contract.scope: cooperating processes on one host, one UID and one private gate root for one candidate schedule
local_contract.first_arm_of_later_block_waits_for: publication of first arms of all earlier blocks
local_contract.next_arm_waits_for: completed or truncated terminal of preceding arm
local_contract.external_failure: stops this block; no retry transition implemented

adversarial_reproductions_and_repairs: Four blocks with completed first arms still counted as open; a fifth first arm was previously accepted when only active run claims were counted. The new replay rejects it until a block closes.
A claim for block 1 without publication previously allowed a claim for block 2. The new order check requires the earlier first arm to be published.
A partial release directory previously accepted a locally declared completed terminal. Marking published and closing terminal now require a verified release manifest and bytes.

If manifest cleanup failed after a preflight error, verify_release could see a valid residual manifest and stage could proceed on the pending claim. An explicit durable published event now blocks staging and terminal until the completed preflight records it.
A caller could mutate the schedule object after claim and before manifest creation, yielding a successful but unverifiable release. Preflight now uses one private snapshot throughout.

An invalid first claim previously left a newly created empty gate root, preventing later valid work. The root now durably initializes an empty state before claim validation; an already-existing empty or damaged root remains blocked.

Completed terminal evidence without artifact_sha256 and external_failure without incident_sha256 could previously advance or close the local block. These fields are now structurally required in line with the receipt auditor.

independent_review.result: The reproduced false-green paths above were closed. No further bypass was found in the cooperating local flow after claim, publication, terminal, sequence, cap, and failure retests.
independent_review.artifact_limit: manifest.json and stage.json are byte-identical in gated and explicit development modes; registry plus exact release path is required to audit local gate use.
independent_review.authority_limit: Terminal status, artifact/incident/trace digests and receipt bytes remain local declarations. This gate does not authenticate provider activity or verify the claimed artifact and trace bytes.
independent_review.filesystem_limit: Visible partial bytes can exist before published, and a same-UID writer can rewrite local registry/evidence or move directories. No independent custody, isolation or cross-host limit is established.

gates.command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_stage_released_run.py tests/test_verify_staged_run.py tests/test_run_staged_local_tool.py tests/test_staged_tool_session.py tests/test_local_run_admission.py
ruff check affected Python files; python -m py_compile core and integrations; git diff --check

limits: The prior MCP same-UID relocation boundary remains the one strict expected failure in the global suite; it is unrelated to this block gate.
No attempt 2 or shared ten-retry allowance is implemented. An external_failure stops its block and leaves later arms missing.
A schedule, root, terminal evidence and provider receipt under the same UID are not independently sealed or authenticated; the gate cannot support a confirmatory criterion-4 claim.
This is a structural development control, not an execution of the proposed matrix, a model comparison, human review or field trial.
